shared_elements: low relief carved on a flat rectangular stone surface
animal forms (bird-like and quadruped shapes in B; winged/feathered forms in A)
a horizontal band or register of repeated small motifs (inscription band in A, row of shapes and toothed band in B)
raised outlines with flat interior modelling
justification: Both are rectangular stone panels worked in low relief with profile-viewed figures and at least one horizontal band of repeated small motifs running across the surface, which is the most concrete correspondence. Otherwise they diverge sharply: A is dominated by a single large, densely detailed human-bodied winged figure with finely incised feathers, hair and plant scrolls, while B is a coarse, schematic assembly of small animal shapes scattered over stacked registers with no dominant figure.
